A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLaID++ research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MP-20 crystal-generation experiments, DPO ablations, space-group-conditioned generation, and DFT validation of generated structures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports coordinate-model iteration results and a compositional UMAP analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions use Qwen-2.5 7B, the same Wyckoff encoding, stability/novelty/space-group preference construction, iterative DPO, and increasing sampling temperatures. v2 reorganizes and motivates these components without establishing a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training remains on MP-20, including the same infilling and property-conditioned prompts. Evaluation retains unconditional generation and the same seven space groups. The new UMAP analysis examines generated materials within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all seven external baselines. Figure 3 drops the separate joint-training/stability-only comparison and revises the unconditional-only control; its no-dynamic-temperature curve matches the former stability-plus-novelty curve. Figure 4 labels its changed third series unconditional-only while the text still describes conditional-only training, leaving that comparator's identity unresolved.

E3.justification: Figure 3 now reports a seven-iteration unconditional-only control where v1 showed a four-iteration unconditional stability-only control. Figure 5 introduces compositional projection and element-based grouping using UMAP. Main evaluation metrics, sample counts, and the documented training and DFT settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the investigation of diversity and collapse: new Table 2 tracks coordinate-based DPO across iterations, Figure 5 examines compositional clusters and P-block metalloid content, and Figure 3 revises the joint-training ablation. The earlier space-group distribution analysis is retained in Appendix 7.3; its relocation is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run averages, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. The existing MLIP-versus-DFT regression and classification reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and DFT validation results are unchanged. New Table 2 reports S.U.N. rates of 2.93%, 2.23%, and 1.69%, alongside stability rates of 10.35%, 13.47%, and 15.94%. Figure 3 revises the unconditional-control trajectory, Figure 4 changes its ambiguously identified third series, and Figure 5 adds qualitative compositional findings. These do not establish improved flagship performance.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit crystal-tuple definition and general KL-regularized expected-reward optimization problem displayed in v1 Equations 1–2. This is a limited reduction in formal background; the DPO loss, Algorithm 1, and appendix Wyckoff mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions refocus on diversity-aware reinforcement learning, representation-dependent collapse, and mutually beneficial joint training in sparse regimes. The central generation and state-of-the-art claims remain. The introduction's greater-than-20% S.U.N. advantage becomes approximately 50%, aligning with v1's existing abstract and results.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new UMAP clusters as evidence of local exploration, preferential P-block metalloid generation, and generalization beyond memorization. It strengthens the representation-collapse interpretation. Much of the physical-prior explanation already appeared in v1 Appendix 7.2, and the principal dataset, objective, and RL-method limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer and per-space-group training counts in Figure 4. Hyperparameters, hardware, relaxation settings, and DFT details are retained. The encoding-length statistics move from the appendix into the method section rather than becoming newly disclosed results.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Bitter Lesson/scaling analogy and its citations, plus the dedicated discussion of WyCryst, Crystal-GFN, and SymmCD. It adds the UMAP citation. Most materials-generation positioning remains, including the DiffCSP++ comparison elsewhere; the citation-style conversion itself is presentational.

P1.justification: The abstract is extensively rewritten, background explanations are substantially condensed, and DPO and Wyckoff method subsections exchange order. Representation motivation moves into the main narrative, while space-group distribution discussion moves to the appendix. Contributions, headings, and citation style are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and figure sizing, splits Figure 3 into two panels, revises Figure 4's labels and adds training counts, and inserts a new table and two-panel UMAP figure. The former Figure 5 moves to the appendix. Other graphics, including the pipeline and generated-crystal examples, are retained.

improvement.justification: The added collapse trajectories, compositional analysis, and code pointer offer useful support and documentation. However, Figure 4's legend contradicts its stated training condition, Figure 5's caption names a different baseline from its legend and discussion, and Table 2's 15.94% coordinate-DPO stability differs from Table 1's 13.94% without explanation. Relevant related-work discussion is also removed. With the principal benchmark and DFT evidence unchanged, these unresolved problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
